hypothesis: A rolled cylinder has zero Gaussian curvature, so its Jacobi transfer equals the plate's, while its extrinsic curvature makes marker chords shorter than geodesic distances by d^3/(24 R^2) + O(d^5).
input_data: Declared tube R = 100 mm, length 300 mm, three rings of 12 markers
Declared instruments (camera 0.02 mm, tracker 0.015 mm, CMM 0.002 mm)
mathematical_model: Cylinder X(phi, z) = (R cos phi, R sin phi, z), R = 100 mm; development (R phi, z) is an isometry; gap(d) = d - 2 R sin(d / 2R) for circumferential pairs; resolvable arc solves gap(d) = k sqrt(2) u.
numerical_result: gap at 90 deg = 15.6583 mm (chord 141.421 vs geodesic 157.080); minimum resolvable arc: camera 23.9 mm, tracker 21.7 mm, CMM 11.1 mm.
observation_model: No observation. The protocol specifies marker, tape start-pose and tape centreline measurements; the hardware slot is empty.
